material_units.source_text:
Theorem — Law of large numbers (statement)
      If $X_1,X_2,\dots$ are i.i.d. with $\mathbb E|X_1|\lt\infty$ and mean $m$, the sample mean $\bar X_N=\tfrac1N\sum_{i=1}^NX_i$ converges to $m$ almost surely (strong law). If also $\operatorname{Var}X_1\lt\infty$, the weak law $\mathbb P(|\bar X_N-m|\gt t)\to0$ for every $t\gt0$ follows from Chebyshev's inequality (Section 5).
